sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Corporate Scope 1-3 Carbon Footprint Auditing and Offset Brokerage

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), subject to its applicable sectoral arrangements
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement, subject to the applicable cross-Strait administrative framework
No generally operative conventional Taiwan–Mainland China bilateral investment treaty or comprehensive double-taxation agreement should be assumed without transaction-specific confirmation
Taiwan's treaties and arrangements with third countries must be reviewed separately for investment protection, withholding tax, and permanent-establishment consequences

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Act (Taiwan), including Articles 7 and 8; Company Act, including Article 22-1 and related company-information reporting obligations; Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Financial Institutions; Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Businesses and Persons at High Risk of Money Laundering or Terrorist Financing; Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Designated Nonfinancial Businesses and Professions, where applicable; Ministry of Economic Affairs rules governing company registration and reporting of company information. Taiwan does not operate a fully public, general-purpose UBO register. Covered entities must identify and verify the natural persons who ultimately own or control the customer, and corporate information may be reported to or obtained by competent authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Mainland China investor certificate of incorporation, business licence, and current corporate registry extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Market Regulation Administration or competent corporate registry in Mainland China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait authentication through the designated Mainland China notarial and Taiwan-side verification mechanism; Hague Apostille and ordinary Taiwan consular legalization should not be assumed to apply

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Mainland China investor board or shareholder resolution approving the Taiwan investment and appointing the authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's governing body, with notarization by a Mainland China notary where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait authentication through the designated Mainland China notarial and Taiwan-side verification mechanism

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, ownership chart, and control-person identification package
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor and each relevant natural-person UBO; supporting registry records issued by competent authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and cross-border authentication appropriate to the document's place of issuance; Hague Apostille is unavailable for Mainland China–Taiwan documents unless a separate legally recognized route applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign natural-person director, representative, and UBO passport copy and address evidence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority and regulated financial institution, public utility, or government authority issuing address evidence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus apostille or consular legalization according to the issuing country's status and Taiwan's acceptance rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Taiwan company name and business-scope pre-check approval and incorporation application documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent local company registration authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Taiwan administrative filing; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and continuously thereafter, screen all shareholders, directors, officers, authorized representatives, signatories, UBOs, major counterparties, banks, and intermediaries against United Nations Security Council sanctions, Taiwan domestic sanctions and counter-terrorism lists, OFAC lists where a US nexus exists or risk-based policy requires, and relevant foreign sanctions lists. Conduct PEP, family-member, close-associate, adverse-media, corruption, proliferation-financing, and sanctions-evasion screening. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, opaque ownership, Mainland China state-linked entities, nominee arrangements, high-risk jurisdictions, unexplained wealth, unusual payment routes, and carbon-credit transactions lacking verifiable provenance. Obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, document risk scoring, and escalate potential matches before account opening or payment execution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce Company and Business Registration Information Inquiry and Online Application System (公司及商業登記查詢及申請服務), generally accessed through https://gcis.nat.gov.tw
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must comply with Taiwan Company Act naming rules and be expressed in Chinese characters. An English name may be registered or used as an auxiliary name subject to administrative acceptance, but it does not replace the mandatory Chinese registered name. The proposed name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and may not mislead the public regarding business type, governmental status, regulated activities, or corporate affiliation. Business items must be selected or described consistently with the official business classification and the actual intended activities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying government, public authority, official status, or state ownership without legal authorization
Words implying banking, insurance, securities, finance, trust, investment, credit, payment, or other regulated financial activity without the required approval
Words implying a licensed professional practice, including legal, accounting, audit, engineering, medical, or other regulated services, without the required qualification or license
Words that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, trademark, governmental body, or well-known enterprise
Words contrary to public order, good morals, or mandatory company-name restrictions
Carbon exchange, emissions trading, verification, certification, or offset-related terms where their use could imply an accredited statutory verification or trading function not actually authorized
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a company-name and business-scope pre-check before incorporation filing. If rejected, review the electronic or written reason, revise the Chinese name or business items, and resubmit through the competent company-registration authority. If the applicant considers the rejection unlawful or factually erroneous, file a written administrative statement or petition for reconsideration with the issuing authority and, where applicable, an administrative appeal under Taiwan administrative-remedy procedures. Preserve the application record, registry search results, supporting trademark or affiliation evidence, authorization documents, and proof of filing. A rejected name should not be used in contracts, invoices, bank onboarding, or public marketing before approval. The stated 180-day period must be confirmed against the current electronic approval notice because the operative period is determined by the issued pre-check approval.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered address in Taiwan is mandatory. A virtual-office or serviced-office arrangement may be accepted for registration if the applicant has a genuine right to use the premises, the landlord permits company registration, and the address satisfies local zoning and registration requirements. It is unsuitable as the sole substance for a business presenting itself as an accredited carbon-verification body, conducting regulated professional work, maintaining employees, storing records, or undertaking material client operations. The company should maintain accessible books and records, competent personnel, decision-making evidence, customer files, AML records, contracts, and operational capability in Taiwan. Scope 1–3 carbon accounting advisory is generally not itself a statutory audit licence, but independent greenhouse-gas verification, certification, emissions-trading, and offset activities may require accreditation, registration, approval, or use of an accredited verification body under Taiwan climate and emissions rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Indicative annual probability of an unannounced or short-notice address verification: approximately 5%–15% for a low-risk advisory company with complete filings and credible local substance; approximately 20%–40% where the entity uses a high-volume virtual office, has Mainland China ownership, has no employees or operating records, receives foreign wires inconsistent with its stated scope, or engages in carbon-credit brokerage or regulated verification. These are risk estimates, not statutory probabilities. The competent authority may inspect or request evidence without prior notice where compliance concerns arise.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taiwan company-name and business-scope pre-check filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent company-registration authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative filing fee; amount varies by electronic or paper filing and current tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent local company-registration authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee based on filing method and capital or registration particulars

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taiwan company seal, representative seal, and statutory filing stamp package
Mainland China corporate registry extracts, notarial certificates, and investor resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Mainland China notary office and competent corporate registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Applicable notarial and document-production charges; market estimate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated cross-Strait document-verification channels and service providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing administrative and professional-service benchmark; varies by document count and urgency

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation of Mainland China corporate, UBO, and constitutional documents into Chinese or English as required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark based on language pair, page count, and certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taiwan attorney or accountant incorporation and foreign-investment filing support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan law firm, accounting firm, or corporate-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional-fee benchmark; not a statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign-investment review, Mainland China investment eligibility analysis, and sectoral business-scope memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan counsel and, where required, Investment Commission or competent authority filing channel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO tracing, ownership-chart verification, PEP and sanctions screening, and adverse-media due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Specialist compliance provider or legal adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; increased for multilayer or state-linked ownership

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office or serviced-office setup and initial address-use deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial rent and service benchmark; location-dependent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial AML/CFT, UBO, sanctions, PEP, source-of-funds, and record-retention policy package
Initial corporate bank or payment-account compliance onboarding support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan bank or payment institution and professional adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Banks generally do not charge a standard incorporation fee; amount represents advisory and documentation support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency for additional document legalization, registry queries, resubmission, and certified copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Relevant authorities, notaries, authentication channels, and professional advisers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency based on prevailing transaction complexity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法) as amended, Articles 128-145 (Company Limited by Shares), Article 387 (Registration), Article 129 (Mandatory Articles of Incorporation Contents); Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例) Articles 3, 7, and 10 (Foreign Investment Approval); Company Registration Rules (公司登記辦法).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (經濟部商業發展署)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company Limited by Shares (股份有限公司設立登記申請書) together with Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) and the minutes of the inaugural shareholders' meeting.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed after the 2009 Company Act reform. The capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully subscribed and the paid-in amount remitted into a designated temporary bank account before filing; capital adequacy for the planned business scope is verified by the Investment Commission in the foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the founding shareholders of the Company that: (1) the subscription of ordinary shares by each founding member identified in the subscription schedule is hereby ratified, and the paid-in capital shall be deposited in a designated temporary bank account; (2) the registered office of the Company shall be located at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, Taiwan; (3) the following persons are hereby appointed as the first officers: [name] as Chairman and Chief Representative, [name] as General Manager, and [name] as Corporate Secretary; and (4) the Chairman is authorized to execute the incorporation application, hire domiciliary advisors, and take all necessary steps to complete corporate registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Online Company Registration Portal (公司登記主題網)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the MOEA online portal and submit the name and business scope pre-approval application, entering the proposed Chinese and English company names, selecting the business scope code corresponding to ISIC 7020 and ESG carbon advisory services, and declaring that the name does not infringe any registered trademark. The pre-approval reserves the name for six months and must match exactly the name used in the later incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Company name and business scope pre-approval application form
Notarized photocopies of government-issued IDs or passports of all founding shareholders
Power of attorney and attorney's ID, if an agent files on behalf of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identical or confusing similarity, file an amended pre-approval with a proposed alternate name without new filing fee provided the application is corrected within 15 days; if the business scope is deemed unclear, submit a narrower scope description and re-submit online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (經濟部投資審議司)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investment application before incorporation is registered. Provide the shareholding breakdown between the Chinese Jiangsu parent, other foreign investors, and the domestic Taiwan partner, the capital remittance schedule, and evidence of the foreign investor's lawful existence. The Commission will assess sector eligibility, national security concerns, and capital adequacy; the approval letter must be presented at company registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment application form (FIA-1)
Draft Articles of Incorporation with share allocation and classes of shares
Business plan, target market analysis, and projected capital utilization schedule
Audited financial statements of each foreign investor for the latest fiscal year
Company registration certificate or equivalent good-standing certificate of the foreign investor, notarized and apostilled
Bank reference letter and remittance instructions for the temporary capital account
Power of attorney in favor of the local incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commission issues a deficiency letter, the applicant has 30 days to submit supplemental explanatory documents; for a rejection on capital adequacy grounds, revise the capital contribution schedule and refile; a negative foreign investment decision is administratively appealable to the Executive Yuan within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration and Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration e-Service (公司登記線上申辦系統)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Commission approval, execute the Articles of Incorporation, hold the inaugural shareholders' meeting to elect directors and a supervisor, and open the temporary capital account. After the paid-in capital is deposited, obtain a bank capital verification certificate and file the registration application electronically with all attachments. Upon approval, the Company will be assigned a Unified Business Number and issued the Certificate of Incorporation (公司登記證明書).
required_dossiers: Application for company registration
Articles of Incorporation signed by all subscribing shareholders
Minutes of the inaugural shareholders' meeting and the first board of directors meeting
Certificate of company name pre-approval
Foreign investment approval letter from the Investment Commission
Bank capital verification certificate evidencing full deposit of paid-in capital
Copy of the registered office lease agreement or certificate of ownership
Photocopies of national IDs or passports of directors, supervisor, and chairman
Written consent to appointment signed by each director and supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure the identified defects via the e-filing system within 15 days; if the fee payment fails, re-upload the payment receipt; any rejection based on capital insufficiency or invalid articles may be cured by a shareholders' special resolution and re-filing accompanied by a fresh capital verification certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Uniform Invoice Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the competent region, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (財政部各地區國稅局)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, the responsible person shall appear in person or via authorized agent at the regional National Taxation Bureau to complete registration for the Business Tax identification (Unified Business Number), register the company seal impression, and apply for issuance of uniform invoices (統一發票). The company must also complete its profit-seeking enterprise income tax file registration under Business Tax Act Article 28.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Tax registration application form signed by the responsible person
Articles of Incorporation and evidence of registered office
Photocopy of the responsible person's ID and company seal card
Certificate of bank account opening
Lease agreement of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau identifies missing documentation, provide the supplement within 14 days; exemption from building-use change tax applies to office uses; if uniform invoice printing is questioned, apply for pre-printed invoice serial numbers via the e-invoice platform.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Labor Insurance, Health Insurance, Fire Safety, and Occupational Post-Registration Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor (勞動部勞工保險局); Ministry of Health and Welfare National Health Insurance Administration; local fire authority and labor inspection agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 8 days after hiring its first employee, the Company must enroll in labor insurance, labor pension, and national health insurance at the competent bureau in the Taipei office district. Simultaneously, the Company must submit a self-fire-safety declaration and obtain the fire safety inspection certificate for the office premises, and file the mandatory occupational hazard prevention plan under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. These clearances are not conditions precedent to incorporation but are required before commencing physical operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Unified Business Number
Company seal and responsible person's seal registration card
Labor insurance enrollment forms and employee roster
National health insurance enrollment forms
Fire safety equipment inspection report for the registered office
Self-fire-safety declaration form (自衛消防編組計畫)
Occupational hazard prevention and emergency response plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing of labor insurance results in administrative penalty; a fire safety inspection failure can be cured by installing required fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and smoke detectors and requesting re-inspection within 30 days; occupational plan deficiencies may be corrected by consulting an accredited industrial safety expert.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (環境部) and its local Environmental Protection Bureaus for GHG verification body accreditation and waste generator registration; the entity otherwise functions under general commercial law without an industrial operating permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Voluntary Greenhouse Gas Verification Body Accreditation (溫室氣體查驗機構認證) under the Climate Change Response Act, applicable only if the Company provides statutory ISO 14064-1 verification statements; no mandatory operating license applies to ISIC 7020 management consulting activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (環境部) with local County/City Environmental Protection Bureau enforcement for annex operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA; the activity is an office-based professional service not listed in the EIA Act schedules. The registered office must, however, register as a general waste generator (一般事業廢棄物) if it produces minor office waste requiring disposal manifests.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office sanitary wastewater discharged into municipal sewers must comply with the Water Pollution Control Act discharge limitations applicable to indirect discharge at the public treatment works (COD ≤ 300 mg/L, SS ≤ 150 mg/L, pH 6-9 at sampling point). VOC emissions from cleaning solvents are de minimis and exempt from air pollution fees; waste batteries, electronic media, and alkaline batteries from audit instruments must be recycled and recorded per the Waste Disposal Act Articles 15 and 36, with a manifest retained for at least 5 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval under Articles 6 and 10 of the Fire Services Act: the office must maintain valid fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, escape route signage, and an automatic alarm system for floor area exceeding 500 m², evidenced by a fire safety equipment inspection certificate from the local fire department. Building usage compliance clearance through the local construction authority ensures the office unit is legally permitted for A-2 or G-2 business occupancy and passes structural load inspection. Occupational Safety and Health Act compliance requires a workplace emergency plan, hazard communication training, and a general safety inspection before onboarding staff; labor inspections are conducted by the local Labor Inspection Office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan), Taxation Administration, together with the Regional National Taxation Bureau having territorial jurisdiction over the JV's registered office; online taxpayer portal at https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the Sino-Foreign Equity JV incorporation with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Commercial and Industrial Registration; the company registration system allocates an 8-digit Unified Business Number (統一編號/UBI) at incorporation. Step 2: Prior to the actual commencement of business, submit the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Tax Registration Form (營利事業設立登記申請書) to the local National Taxation Bureau, attaching the company registration certificate, MOEA investment approval, Articles of Incorporation, responsible person identification, business premises title or lease, and bank account evidence. Step 3: The National Taxation Bureau enrolls the JV as a business taxpayer, records the VAT/Business Tax status, and approves the Uniform Invoice serial-number range. Step 4: For foreign shareholders, the JV also files withholding tax registration (扣繳單位設立登記) for payments subject to withholding. Step 5: Update tax registration within the statutory period after any change in name, business scope, responsible person, or premises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The domestic Sino-Foreign Equity JV Ltd is a ROC tax-resident profit-seeking enterprise; it is neither a pass-through nor a disregarded entity. It files Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax on worldwide net income at a flat entity rate of 20% and is subject to the Alternative Minimum Tax where applicable. A branch of a foreign enterprise is taxed only on Taiwan-source income if the head office is outside Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch entity election is available under Taiwan tax law. A Taiwan-incorporated JV has no mechanism to elect transparent pass-through treatment. Group consolidation is not recognized; each company is a standalone taxpayer. A foreign enterprise may choose to operate through a branch rather than a subsidiary, but that choice is made through corporate documentation and does not constitute a tax entity classification election. Certain taxpayers meeting the small-scale threshold may elect simplified gross-receipts business tax treatment, and exporters may elect periodic input VAT refund procedures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax under the Business Tax Act (加值型營業稅), a credit-method VAT with zero-rating for exports and exemptions for specified financial and professional services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: TWD 0 for domestic businesses: tax registration is mandatory before commencement of a taxable activity with no economic turnover exemption. Small-scale businesses with average monthly taxable sales below TWD 200,000 may be subject to a simplified 1% (goods) or 2% (services) gross-receipts business tax. Non-resident suppliers of cross-border electronic or offshore services to Taiwan become registrable VAT taxpayers when annual taxable sales exceed TWD 480,000; below that threshold, imported services are generally subject to reverse-charge Business Tax at 5%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates Uniform Invoices (統一發票) for registered VAT businesses. Electronic invoices must be transmitted to the eGUI Integrated Service Platform (電子發票整合服務平台) using Turnkey software or approved APIs; Uniform Invoice numbers and random codes are system-generated from eGUI. There is no per-invoice cryptographic real-time clearance, but invoice data must be uploaded within prescribed windows (generally 48 hours for B2C invoices and 7 days for B2B invoices) and retained on the platform for statutory periods; void and blank invoice controls also require same-channel reporting. Export invoices must carry a zero-rated tax code and be retained in the invoice book with supporting export documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Business Tax Act Article 7 for goods physically exported from Taiwan and for services sold to foreign enterprises or persons where the service is used or consumed outside Taiwan or is necessary for export. For ESG carbon footprint auditing, offset brokerage and carbon advisory services to be zero-rated, the service recipient must be a non-Taiwan enterprise, the engagement must evidence offshore performance or offshore use, and the payment must be received in foreign currency from outside Taiwan; services rendered physically in Taiwan or benefiting Taiwan-based operations do not qualify and must be taxed at 5%. The registered JV must issue a zero-rated Uniform Invoice, report the export sales in the VAT return, and substantiate any input VAT refund claim with export or offshore-service documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) with customs serial number and exporter Unified Business Number for goods; for offshore services, a signed engagement agreement with the foreign recipient and statement of offshore delivery in lieu of a customs declaration
Commercial invoice and zero-rated tax invoice
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international freight carrier evidence showing physical departure from Taiwan for goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (銀行水單/匯入匯款通知書) showing remittance from the non-Taiwan customer
Carbon audit service work papers, GHG verification evidence, deliverable acceptance report, and proof of actual use of the service outside Taiwan
Export sales ledger and reconciliation file enabling tie-back to the relevant VAT return and customs data
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau scrutinizes zero-rating claims through post-return VAT audits, cross-checking customs declarations, foreign exchange settlement certificates, and bank remittance records. If zero-rating is claimed without actual export or with fabricated foreign exchange receipts, the tax authority reassesses the sales as taxable at 5%, with daily interest, and imposes a Business Tax Act Article 51 penalty of up to five times the underpaid tax; fraudulent export documents may trigger penal tax evasion proceedings under the Tax Collection Act, denial of refund, revocation of invoice registration, and, for goods-related false declarations, Customs Act penalties. Claims are retroactively reviewable for five years from filing, or seven years in cases involving fraudulent concealment, and refunds already paid are clawed back with mandatory interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), principally through its Department of Foreign Exchange. The principal framework includes the Foreign Exchange Control Act, the Regulations Governing Foreign Exchange Business of Banking Enterprises, and related Central Bank circulars. Investment approval and foreign-investment registration may additionally involve Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Investment Promotion. For a mainland-China-linked investor, the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area and related regulations impose additional approval, ownership, funding, and transaction restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is not fully freely convertible. Current-account transactions are generally permitted through authorized banks, subject to genuine-trade documentation, foreign-exchange declarations, anti-money-laundering controls, and applicable transaction thresholds. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity, shareholder loans, outbound investment, guarantees, and certain intercompany financing, require registration, approval, or reporting depending on the transaction and investor status. A foreign-invested Taiwan company may generally remit dividends, liquidation proceeds, interest, and principal after satisfaction of tax, corporate-law, audited-financial-statement, foreign-investment-registration, and bank-documentation requirements. Dividend remittance normally requires evidence of distributable profits, shareholder approval, tax filing or withholding, and relevant investment registration. A mainland-China investor or mainland-controlled structure is subject to materially higher legal risk: investment, ownership, management participation, funding, technology transfer, and related-party transactions may require prior approval or may be prohibited. The proposed ESG carbon-accounting and offset-brokerage activities should be screened separately for regulated professional services, environmental-commodity, securities, futures, payment, and brokerage implications even though ordinary advisory services may not require a general statutory business license.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not generally impose a universal statutory requirement that exporters surrender or convert a fixed percentage of export proceeds into New Taiwan dollars. Export proceeds may generally be received in foreign currency or converted through an authorized foreign-exchange bank. The exporter must maintain commercial evidence, including contracts, invoices, shipping or service-delivery records, customs or electronic export records where applicable, bank remittance data, and transaction-purpose information. Foreign-exchange declarations and Central Bank reporting apply when statutory thresholds, transaction types, or annual cumulative limits are exceeded; the applicable threshold must be confirmed with the servicing bank at execution because Central Bank rules and administrative limits may change. Banks may require receipt of proceeds through an authorized bank, reconciliation of outstanding export advances, and explanations for delayed receipt, third-party payment, netting, factoring, or offset arrangements. No fixed conversion ratio should be assumed. Proceeds related to carbon credits, environmental attributes, brokerage commissions, or advisory services should be classified accurately because they may not qualify as ordinary merchandise exports and may attract enhanced source-of-funds and transaction-purpose review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Account or Foreign-Investment Funding Account, together with a New Taiwan dollar Operational Account and Foreign-Currency Operational Account
Capital Account or Foreign-Investment Funding Account, New Taiwan dollar Operational Account, Foreign-Currency Operational Account, and Trade-Settlement Account
Capital Funding Account, New Taiwan dollar Operational Account, Foreign-Currency Operational Account, and Treasury or Hedging Account
Capital Funding Account, New Taiwan dollar Operational Account, Foreign-Currency Operational Account, and Trade-Settlement Account
Capital Funding Account, New Taiwan dollar Operational Account, Foreign-Currency Operational Account, and Treasury Account
Capital Funding Account, New Taiwan dollar Operational Account, Foreign-Currency Operational Account, and Trade-Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment initiation and limited operational collection; Low for replacing a Taiwan-authorized corporate bank account. An offshore electronic-money institution cannot automatically accept deposits, operate payment accounts, provide regulated remittance services, or conduct foreign-exchange business in Taiwan without the required Taiwan licensing, local-partner structure, and regulatory permissions. Offshore EMI balances may be treated by Taiwan banks as third-party funds or higher-risk payment flows. The company should use a Taiwan-authorized bank for capital injection, payroll, taxes, dividends, and material customer receipts. Any payment intermediary must be screened for licensing, beneficial ownership, safeguarding, sanctions, correspondent-bank access, data-transfer controls, transaction limits, and prohibition on undisclosed nested payment activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding may be available for selected Taiwan-incorporated companies and existing institutional customers, but it is not a guaranteed legal entitlement. Banks commonly require in-person or enhanced video identification for directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, and controlling persons, particularly for a newly incorporated entity, foreign shareholders, mainland-China links, cross-border consulting receipts, carbon-credit transactions, or unusual ownership chains. Original or certified corporate documents, Taiwan tax and registration records, foreign-investment approval or registration, specimen signatures, board resolutions, and source-of-funds evidence may be required. The bank may require a Taiwan-resident contact, local operating address, evidence of actual business, and post-opening verification. A mainland-China shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner should be disclosed fully; concealment or nominee arrangements create severe account-rejection, freezing, and regulatory risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mainland-China shareholder, director, controller, lender, guarantor, or ultimate beneficial owner without evidence of required Taiwan approval.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents; complete ownership chart to natural persons; passports and residential evidence; mainland and Taiwan investment approvals; Department of Investment Promotion records; cross-strait regulatory filings; board and shareholder resolutions; beneficial-owner declarations; sanctions screening; legal memorandum confirming permitted ownership and activities; and a transaction map identifying all mainland-connected funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent or incomplete beneficial-ownership chain, nominee ownership, trust arrangement, or unexplained intermediary holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart; registers of members and directors; certified corporate extracts; shareholder agreements; trust or nominee declarations where legally permitted; ultimate-owner identity records; independent corporate registry searches; tax-residency certificates; and a signed ownership-and-control certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a third-party account, offshore payment platform, related party not shown in corporate records, or an account in a different jurisdiction from the investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed investment agreement; approved capital plan; bank statements; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; investor financial statements; board resolutions; remittance instruction; purpose-code explanation; relationship disclosure; and written confirmation that the remitter is the approved investor or an expressly documented financing entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business described as carbon trading, offset brokerage, environmental-attribute dealing, or financial investment rather than advisory and audit services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Precise business-scope memorandum; service agreements; sample invoices; customer and supplier due diligence; carbon-standard and registry information; explanation of whether the company takes title to credits; confirmation that it does not provide securities, futures, investment-management, payment, or deposit-taking services; regulatory perimeter opinion; and transaction-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border receipts inconsistent with a low-risk ESG advisory profile, including circular flows, rapid pass-through, cash withdrawals, or extensive third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling cash-flow forecast; customer concentration analysis; signed contracts; invoices; deliverables; timesheets; project reports; bank reconciliation; expected jurisdictions and currencies; explanation of payment terms; approval matrix; and documented prohibition on personal accounts, cash settlement, and unapproved third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Carbon-credit or offset proceeds with uncertain title, registry provenance, sanctions exposure, double counting, fraud, or environmental-claim risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry account records; project documentation; issuance and retirement certificates; chain-of-title evidence; contractual warranties; sanctions and adverse-media screening; beneficial-owner checks for project counterparties; verification or validation reports; anti-double-counting controls; and legal review of marketing claims.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to demonstrate local substance, including no employees, no premises, no management activity, or no credible operating plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Office lease or service-office agreement; employment records; payroll plan; director and management biographies; local contracts; operating budget; tax registration; website and professional credentials; board minutes; and a twelve-month activity forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for unrestricted online banking, payment aggregation, virtual accounts, or account access by non-resident group personnel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Delegation-of-authority policy; board-approved banking mandate; user-access matrix; dual-control procedures; device and authentication controls; transaction limits; periodic access review; group treasury policy; and documented separation between payment initiation and approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual foreign-exchange activity, including repeated conversions without commercial rationale, speculative positions, unexplained NDF activity, or mismatches between invoices and remittance currencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved FX policy; exposure schedule; underlying invoices and contracts; hedge-designation records; board or treasury approvals; counterparty confirmations; valuation reports; hedge accounting documentation where applicable; and reconciliation of each hedge to an identified receivable, payable, or forecast exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax, accounting, or corporate records inconsistent with banking declarations, including missing audited accounts or unresolved related-party balances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Taiwan tax registration; tax filings; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements where applicable; general ledger; trial balance; related-party register; transfer-pricing documentation; intercompany agreements; management representation; and remediation plan for historical discrepancies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a Taiwan-authorized bank and obtain any required foreign-investment or cross-strait approval before remittance. The investor should remit from an account in its own legal name to the designated capital-funding account, using the bank's prescribed capital-investment purpose classification and exact beneficiary name. The remittance package should include the investment approval or registration, constitutional documents, subscription or joint-venture agreement, board and shareholder resolutions, capital schedule, remitter identity, source-of-funds evidence, and bank confirmation of the capital-account treatment. The receiving bank should verify the investor, beneficial owners, purpose, amount, currency, and ownership allocation before crediting or converting the funds. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated group entities, offshore EMIs, cash, or omnibus payment accounts. After receipt, complete required capital verification, registration, accounting, and tax steps before using funds for operating expenses. Shareholder loans require separate review of foreign-exchange, corporate-law, tax, thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, and cross-strait restrictions. Retain SWIFT messages, bank advice, approval documents, capital verification evidence, and ledger reconciliation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary cross-border services and permitted trade, use a Taiwan-authorized bank through SWIFT customer credit transfer, ordinarily an MT103-equivalent payment message or the bank's ISO 20022 successor. Payment files should state the true beneficiary, underlying contract or invoice number, service or goods description, currency, value date, and transaction purpose. For higher-value or documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank-guaranteed structure subject to UCP 600, ISP98, URC 522, sanctions screening, and the bank's credit approval. ESG advisory fees should be paid against executed engagement letters and deliverables; carbon-credit or offset transactions should include registry, title, retirement, and counterparty documentation. Dividends require distributable-profit evidence, shareholder approval, withholding-tax treatment, audited or accountant-supported financial statements, and investment-registration records. Intercompany service fees, royalties, interest, and management charges require transfer-pricing support, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner review, and evidence of actual services. Banks may reject third-party settlement, netting, round-tripping, split invoices, vague payment descriptions, or payments to high-risk jurisdictions. Maintain maker-checker controls, sanctions screening, invoice-to-bank reconciliation, and payment records for the statutory retention period.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized Taiwan bank, supported by an identifiable underlying receivable, payable, committed transaction, or documented forecast exposure. The company should maintain exposure evidence, maturity limits, counterparty approvals, valuation records, and cancellation or rollover controls.

Foreign-exchange swaps with an authorized bank for documented liquidity or currency-management needs, subject to bank suitability, exposure, collateral, accounting, and foreign-exchange reporting requirements.

Currency options or option combinations, where offered by an authorized bank and appropriate for the company's sophistication, with full disclosure of premium, contingent obligations, leverage, early-termination risk, and worst-case cash requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available through an authorized bank or offshore counterparty, but availability, settlement currency, counterparty jurisdiction, reporting, enforceability, and Taiwan foreign-exchange rules must be confirmed transaction by transaction. NDFs must not be used to evade Taiwan controls or create undisclosed speculative exposure.

Cross-currency swaps or interest-rate and currency-linked derivatives may be used only after bank suitability review, board-approved treasury authorization, documentation of the underlying exposure, collateral and valuation analysis, and confirmation that the transaction is not regulated securities, futures, investment-management, or unauthorized derivative activity.

Prohibited or high-risk practices include naked speculative FX positions, derivative transactions through unlicensed intermediaries, personal-account hedging, undocumented back-to-back trades, concealed third-party funding, and hedges unrelated to the company's approved business or measurable exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report of directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of issued shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronically file within one month before the anniversary date of the company's registration; update changes within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of approximately TWD 50,000 to TWD 500,000, with repeated fines for continued non-compliance; failure may lead to an order to rectify and, after statutory escalation, dissolution or revocation measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements and business report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; filed with the competent authority only where a separate statutory registration or submission is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year, unless a statutory extension or special rule applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may incur administrative fines and liability for breach of the Company Act; persistent failure may trigger corrective orders and further sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally May 1 through May 31 of the following year for a calendar-year taxpayer; the filing period may differ for an approved non-calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in penalties, estimated assessment, tax collection actions, and interest; failure to file may attract a fine generally calculated by reference to tax payable, subject to statutory limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax provisional return or provisional tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally September 1 through September 30 each year for a calendar-year taxpayer, unless an applicable exemption or alternative calculation method applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or insufficient payment may cause additional tax, interest, penalties, and collection measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Normally filed bimonthly by the 15th day of the following odd-numbered month; not an annual filing, but required for annual maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment may result in fines, interest, estimated assessment, and collection enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company internal records; Ministry of Economic Affairs where a statutory electronic report or registration update is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually before the Article 22-1 reporting window and immediately following any ownership, director, manager, or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or report required information may result in administrative fines, repeated daily or periodic penalties, corrective orders, and escalation under the Company Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified public accountant audit and certification is generally required for public companies and for non-public companies meeting applicable statutory thresholds, commonly paid-in capital of at least TWD 30 million, annual net operating revenue of at least TWD 100 million, or total assets of at least TWD 100 million; sector-specific rules may impose additional requirements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies and other designated entities generally apply Taiwan-IFRS; eligible private companies generally apply Taiwan GAAP under the Business Accounting Act and related regulations, unless they elect or are required to use Taiwan-IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Reconcile the ultimate beneficial ownership chain, direct and indirect shareholdings, control rights, directors, supervisors, and managers at least annually; file the statutory annual Article 22-1 report within one month before the company-registration anniversary and update reportable changes within 15 days. Taiwan does not impose a standalone annual UBO certification equivalent to certain foreign jurisdictions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges or Encumbrances over Shares

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 1,000-3,500 annually, depending on location, mail handling, company secretary support, and statutory filing services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-15,000 for a privately held Taiwan company, increasing for foreign-invested joint ventures, complex consolidation, regulated activities, ESG or carbon-accounting evidence, and multi-entity reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan's Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Act sets the statutory rate at 20%. Qualified innovative enterprises and startups under the Company Act and Statute for Industrial Innovation (SII) may enjoy a reduced rate of 15% on their first NT$1.2 million of taxable income, and certain tax credits are available for R&D expenditures, investments in smart machinery and 5G systems, and ESG-related green investments recognized by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. Foreign investment income attributable to a Taiwanese branch may be eligible for domestic dividend participation exemption under Article 42 of the Income Tax Act, subject to the 20% shareholding and one-year holding-period requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form No. 20) filed via the electronic filing system of the Ministry of Finance (申报系统), including the mandatory attachment of the tax audit report, financial statements, and the E-file system (電子申報繳稅服務)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the 5th month after the fiscal year-end (31 May for calendar-year taxpayers); an extension of up to one additional month may be granted upon application, with a maximum extension period of two months for tax return filing and one month for payment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, operating costs, gross profit, operating expenses, non-operating income and expenses, and net profit before tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-invested JV must report all Taiwan-source income on the tax return, including revenue from carbon audit advisory services, offset brokerage commissions, and any ESG project management fees; income realized offshore must be reported only if attributable to a Taiwan permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from book pre-tax profit to taxable income, including permanent differences, temporary differences, investment income exemptions, and loss carryforward deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' undistributed earnings are not deductible; dividends received from a foreign subsidiary may require tracing to the underlying business substance and cannot be sheltered merely by booking through a tax haven

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the 20% statutory rate, applying the NT$120,000 benefit for qualified small enterprises, and deducting foreign tax credits (FTC) with a per-country limitation, investment tax credits, and minimum tax credit under the Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) regime
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are allowed only with a Certificate of Residence and tax payment evidence from the foreign jurisdiction, and only against Taiwan-source or deemed-Taiwan-source income; a CN-HK-TW group structure must allocate profits according to actual economic functions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation account balance, distributable earnings, and shareholder tax credit allocation; for a non-resident corporate shareholder, the withholding tax is credited against the JV's retained earnings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax on dividends paid to the Chinese parent company is subject to Article 25 of the Income Tax Act (21% flat withholding on the gross dividend paid to a non-resident company) unless reduced under the Taiwan-China Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation, in which case the 10% limitation applies conditioned on TRC and beneficial-ownership documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alternative Minimum Tax on corporate taxpayers; AMT base includes taxable income plus certain preference items, including offshore income from a tax haven subsidiary, with a NT$2 million exemption and a 12% rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Chinese JV owns a foreign carbon-offset brokerage subsidiary in a zero-tax jurisdiction, the deemed offshore income may be included in the AMT base; detailed CFC rules under Article 43-4 of the Income Tax Act apply to controlled foreign corporations, unless a substantive business activity test is met

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction schedule (Form 20-1) and transfer pricing report, covering cross-border service transactions, intragroup payment for management fees, IP royalty payments, and financial guarantees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent company must justify all cross-border payments with contemporaneous benchmarking; the JV must file the related-party disclosure when transactions with related parties exceed NT$20 million annually or when the company meets the prescribed entity threshold

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on undistributed surplus: retained earnings at year-end exceeding the distributable limit are subject to an additional 5% tax when not distributed in the following year, under Article 66-9 of the Income Tax Act
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent should plan profit distribution to avoid the 5% undistributed-surplus surcharge; a reasonable dividend policy based on substantive cash flows and working capital needs should be documented to withstand challenge

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a surcharge of 3% of the overdue tax amount for each two-month period, up to a maximum of 30%, plus interest at the post office one-year fixed deposit rate; failure to file despite demand with intent to evade can result in a penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax or imprisonment up to seven years for egregious tax evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders under Articles 3 and 25 of the Income Tax Act; domestic corporate shareholders receive a full participation exemption subject to the 20% shareholding and one-year holding requirement
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement (海峡两岸避免双重课税及加强税务合作协议), the Chinese parent company must obtain a Certificate of Residence (居住證明) from the tax authority of Mainland China, submit a treaty relief application to the Taiwan tax authority with a beneficial-ownership declaration, and receive approval before the reduced withholding rate of 10% is applied to dividends. The investor must demonstrate substantive business operations and that the JV is not used as a conduit for treaty abuse. Taiwan's domestic law requires the beneficial owner to be the recipient of the income and to have the power to dispose of the dividends; failure to meet the substance condition restores the 21% statutory rate. For tax treaties in general, the Mutual Agreement Procedure and the TRC exchange mechanism under the Taiwan-China agreement are administered by the Taipei National Tax Administration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-resident enterprises are subject to a 20% withholding rate on gross amounts (Article 88 and 92 of the Income Tax Act); under the Cross-Strait Agreement, the royalty withholding rate is reduced to 10% if the beneficial owner is a resident of Mainland China and the IP is not effectively connected with a Taiwan PE. Interest paid to non-resident companies is generally subject to 15% withholding on gross interest, and 20% for short-term promissory note interest; the Cross-Strait Agreement limits interest WHT to 10% if the recipient is the beneficial owner and a mainland China resident. Commissions, fees for technical services and carbon-audit subcontracted fees paid to a non-resident without a PE are characterized as royalties or business profits under Article 25(1), which allows the tax authority to deem 15% of the gross payment as taxable income and impose a 20% income tax (effective 3% on gross), unless a treaty or cross-strait agreement provides a reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Taiwan taxpayer must prepare a transfer pricing report (Local File) if related-party transactions exceed NT$20 million in a year or the company meets the total revenue threshold set by the Ministry of Finance (NT$300 million for the Master File threshold; a Master File is required if the group's annual consolidated revenue exceeds NT$30 billion). In addition, a cross-border related-party service fee exceeding NT$2 million must be supported by a cost/benefit analysis and a written contract.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) codification like the UAE or BVI, but the substance-over-form doctrine is embedded in the Income Tax Act (Articles 43-1, 43-3 and 43-4): Article 43-1 allows revenue authorities to recharacterize transactions with no business purpose; Article 43-3 imposes mandatory transfer pricing disclosure and sets document penalties; Article 43-4 (CFC rules) attributes profits of a low-tax foreign subsidiary to the Taiwanese controlling shareholder when the CFC's effective tax rate is below 14% and it fails the substance test (active business test is not sufficient; the CFC must have substantive establishment in the registered jurisdiction). For a Sino-Foreign JV performing ESG carbon auditing and offset brokerage, the tax authority will scrutinize whether the Taiwan entity has real office premises, full-time qualified professionals (carbon auditors, ESG analysts), a board structure that makes strategic decisions in Taiwan, and contracts executed and invoiced from Taiwan. Pure profit-engineering without local substance triggers the four fatal regimes: deemed capital contribution recharacterization, AMT inclusion, penalty for misreporting, and criminal liability for fraudulent tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a return that omits Taiwan-source service income, inflating deductible carbon-offset brokerage costs, creating false invoices for ESG advisory sub-contracts, or paying fictitious royalties to an affiliated offshore IP holding company in a zero-tax jurisdiction to shift profit out of Taiwan
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Collection Act (稅捐稽徵法) Articles 41 and 47, tax evasion with intent or by fraudulent means triggers a penalty of up to NT$2 million and imprisonment for up to seven years; in addition, the underpaid tax is subject to a penalty of 20% to 100% of the evaded amount, plus daily interest. A false invoice under the Business Tax Act carries a penalty of 5% of the transaction amount per violation, not less than NT$16,000 and not more than NT$1 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the JV can be personally liable for the company's unpaid taxes if they fail to discharge statutory filing duties or cause fraudulent returns to be filed. Under Article 47 of the Tax Collection Act, the responsible person (representative director, general manager, or actual controlling shareholder) is subject to criminal imprisonment even when the company is a legal person. Civilly, a director who approves a dividend distribution while the company is insolvent or without considering the unpaid tax liability may be liable to creditors or the state under the Company Act and the doctrine of piercing the corporate veil; travel bans, denial of visa applications, and seizure of personal assets are administrative enforcement tools under the Tax Collection Act (Article 24).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling carbon auditing services to the Chinese parent or its subsidiaries at below-arm's-length fees, or paying excessive management fees, IP royalties, or interest on shareholder loans to evade proper taxable profit in Taiwan; failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documents when the NT$20 million threshold is crossed; entering into a circular transaction where a Hong Kong or BVI intermediary performs no substantive function in carbon offset brokering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust the taxpayer's income to an arm's-length amount, resulting in additional tax, plus a penalty of 2 times the underpaid tax amount if the taxpayer failed to disclose the related-party transactions correctly (Article 43-3 of the Income Tax Act); in serious manipulation cases, a 30% surcharge on underpaid tax may be imposed, and the CFC rules require the Taiwanese shareholder to include the low-tax foreign company's profits pro rata in current-year income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the related-party transaction schedule knowing that it contains misrepresentations or who approve a cross-border payment without due diligence can be jointly and severally liable for the additional tax and penalty. A director found to have conspired to shift profits to a related shell company may face criminal charges of document forgery and breach of trust under the Criminal Code (Articles 210 and 342), with imprisonment up to five years for breach of trust; an exit or travel ban may be issued against the director during the tax investigation (Article 24(3) of the Tax Collection Act).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Taiwan JV as a mere invoicing vehicle with no staff, no physical office, no Taiwan-based management, and no real operations in carbon audit and offset brokerage; generation of paper-only profit for the purpose of obtaining treaty benefits on intellectual property or fees; misrepresenting the JV as an operating company while the board meetings, decisions, and business activities occur in Hong Kong or Mainland China
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act, the tax authority is empowered to recharacterize and allocate the entire profit to the entity that has actual business substance and economic functions, moving taxable income from Taiwan to the real management jurisdiction; if that jurisdiction is not effectively taxing, the AMT 12% tax applies (or the CFC inclusion rule if a low-tax subsidiary is involved). The 5% undistributed-surplus surcharge may also apply; further, misuse of cross-strait treaty relief results in unilateral denial of the 10% WHT rate and retroactive 21% withholding plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A nominee director who knowingly operates a shell JV can be pursued under the Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法) if funds passing through the JV are the proceeds of tax offenses and are routed via offshore bank accounts, even if the predicate offense was committed in another jurisdiction. Directors could be stripped of their corporate veil protection, ordered to repay the tax deficiency plus penalties jointly and severally, restricted from leaving Taiwan without court or tax authority permission, and subject to criminal imprisonment of up to seven years for tax fraud and up to five years for money laundering; directors' personal bank accounts can be frozen under the Money Laundering Control Act enforcement rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Brokering carbon offsets that originate from entities listed on international sanctions registers, accepting proceeds in cryptocurrency or unregulated payment instruments, or structuring payments into multiple wire transfers below reporting thresholds (smurfing) to avoid the Financial Supervisory Commission's transaction reporting rules; failure to maintain beneficial ownership records of offset sellers and buyers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Money Laundering Control Act (Articles 7, 9, and 18) imposes a fine of up to NT$5 million for failure to maintain AML mechanisms for a low-risk business; for willful concealment of suspicious transactions, imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to NT$50 million; wire transfer reporting thresholds apply to any transfer equal to or above NT$1 million executed through Swift or wire rails if the counterparty is a sanctioned jurisdiction. The capital market regulator can also revoke the company's registration or license for ESG services if it is a member of a professional body.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 8 of the Money Laundering Control Act, a director who instructs or permits non-compliant wire transfers without performing a sanctions screen is subject to a criminal penalty of up to three years; if the director provides false or incomplete customer due diligence records, the prison term is raised to five years and the fine to NT$7 million. Directors can be held civilly liable to the state for any confiscated proceeds; an arrest warrant can be issued for transnational money laundering offenses, and a MoU-based cross-strait law enforcement request can trigger personal asset freezing in Mainland China for the corporate director who is a Chinese citizen.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undistributed Earnings and Dividend Tax Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accumulating earnings in the Taiwan JV without a bona fide business plan to defer the 21% shareholder dividend WHT while also using the accumulated cash balances to fund interest-free shareholder loans or offshore prepayments to the Chinese parent; declaring dividends to a non-resident while failing to withhold 21% WHT (or 10% treaty rate after approval); distribution of dividends funded by non-deductible reserves without financial statement approval by shareholders; use of a HK intermediary to receive Taiwan dividends and re-invoice to the parent at a mark-up in order to avoid the 10% cross-strait dividend limitation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to withhold dividend WHT triggers a penalty of 1.5 times the unwithheld amount (Article 114 of the Income Tax Act); failure to pay the withheld tax on time attracts a daily interest penalty and a surcharge of 10% to 20%; undistributed retained earnings over the distributable threshold are subject to a 5% tax under Article 66-9; if the dividend was artificially structured to avoid WHT, the tax authority may disregard the intermediary, impute the dividend to the Chinese parent, and reassess the 21% withholding (with the reduced treaty rate if the parent obtains TRC, but the intermediary's existence alone may invalidate treaty relief and trigger a 20% penalty on the gross amount).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person who knowingly signs a false dividend distribution resolution or gives an instruction to avoid WHT is jointly liable for the withholding tax and penalties under Article 114; such a director may be debarred from acting as a director of any company in Taiwan for up to five years; in cases involving coercive threats or fraud to use offshore nominees to hold dividend rights, imprisonment up to five years applies. Chinese citizens serving as directors of the JV face extradition risk where an MOJ mutual legal assistance request is made for a serious economic crime.
